findings.title: Your 08:12 to Paddington was 38 minutes late: £14.20 to claim
findings.why: Your Trainline ticket shows the 08:12 from Oxford to Paddington on 23 October. It cost £28.40. The rail records say it was 38 minutes late, so you can claim £14.20 back.
findings.say: My 08:12 train from Oxford to Paddington was 38 minutes late on 23 October. It cost £28.40.

findings.title: Did they come? Broadbandly had an engineer booked for 19 October.
findings.why: Your calendar has a Broadbandly engineer booked for 19 October, 8am to 1pm. If no one came, Broadbandly may owe you money for it.
findings.say: The Broadbandly engineer did not come on 19 October. Can you help?

findings.title: The email from “HMRC” is a trick
findings.why: Scam Shield says it is not from HMRC. Do not click its link, reply or pay. If you are not sure, call HMRC on a number you trust.

source.item: Email: HMRC: you are due a tax refund

findings.say: Is this a scam? You are due a tax refund of 248.20 GBP. Claim within 24 hours at http://hmrc-refunds-gov.uk/claim

findings.title: Thames Water paid £23.40 into your bank
findings.why: Your bank shows £23.40 from Thames Water on 9 October. Their email said this money was coming, so there is nothing to do.
